The Independent, published 19 Nov 2026

The former cabinet minister beat Westminster councillor Festus Akinbusoye and Sara Gezdari to win the nomination

Former minister Sir James Cleverly has been selected as the Conservative candidate for the next London mayoral election.

The Braintree MP won in the first round of ballots, gaining 86 per cent of the vote from Conservative Party members. He beat Westminster councillor Festus Akinbusoye, communications professional Alex Challoner, and former parliamentary candidate Sara Gezdari to win the nomination.

Cleverly also confirmed that he would not be seeking re-election as an MP, declaring he was “all in” to fight to become London mayor.

The veteran Tory served as foreign secretary and home secretary in the last Conservative government, before running against Kemi Badenoch for the party leadership in 2024.

The next election for London mayor will take place in 2028 and Cleverly said that the current mayor Lord Sadiq Khan of Tooting is “letting London down”.

“People are leaving London, or not choosing to come here in the first place, businesses, job creators, families leaving London, and by the time of the election in 2028, Khan will have been mayor for 12 years, and those two things are related,” he said.

“The problems London faces are the symptoms. Khan is the cause.

“When I ask Londoners, do you feel safe walking home at night? The answer is no.

“It’s shameful, it’s a failure, and it’s not just crime.

“We have had the worst period of house building since the Second World War and only the highest-earning Londoners can afford the cheapest houses in London.”
